  reaches pc2 with 0% loss and low, stable RTT -- the peering is not congested.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- high latency / congestion on the peering -- is NOT reproducible: pc1
(195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss and low, stable round-trip
time. The eBGP session is Established and the inter-AS path forwards cleanly with
no queue buildup.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: latency is low and stable and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a
sustained ping pc1->pc2, observes low stable RTT, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the peering congested or restarting
router1/router2 to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The routed path between pc1 (195.11.14.2) and the partner LAN host pc2 (200.1.1.2) is healthy. Layer‑3 reachability is clean with low latency and no loss: end‑to‑end pings average ~2 ms with 0% loss (both directions), and path MTU is full 1500 bytes (DF 1472 ping succeeds). Throughput tests between pc1 and pc2 sustain ~70–75 Mbit/s in both directions; only minor TCP retransmissions were observed (78 forward, 2 reverse), which correlate to a small, transient TX drop count (78) on router1 eth0. Queuing is not congested: tc on all path interfaces shows fq_codel with zero drops/overlimits and empty backlogs. Links are up/full duplex at 10G on every hop. Routing is correct and stable: BGP is up on router1↔router2, each advertising its /24 and installing the remote /24 via the inter‑router link.

Mechanism: With no queuing loss or elevated RTT/jitter, the “treacle” experience is not attributable to network congestion or misrouting. The negligible device‑level TX drops on router1 eth0 are too few to explain large slowdowns and did not inflate latency.

Localization: Entire path pc1 → router1 (eth1/eth0) → router2 (eth0/eth1) → pc2 verified normal. On the endpoint, pc2 is not running application listeners (netstat shows no services beyond the local DNS stub), which would make app connections refuse or stall.

Root cause: No network fault found; perceived slowness likely due to the partner application/service on 200.1.1.2, not the transport path.

Corrective fix: No network changes required. Engage the partner/application owner to verify the service is running and responsive on 200.1.1.2; if issues persist, capture SYN/SYN‑ACK timing to confirm app‑layer delay.
